title: Upcoming trip to Europe and a Harry Lim record date
summary: Jones is about to leave for six weeks in Europe, and Hinton mentions an upcoming date with George Barnes produced by Harry Lim.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Coming from you, Jo, thank you. But let's get on with you now because this is so very important, because this is your day and we want these young people, whoever would search out, to know about you and the great things that you've tried to do in the whole taking of this thing. So now we're up to 1972. Here it is 1973 -
And I'm fixing to go to Europe in a few minutes, after I get through talking to you. I'm supposed to join Milt Buckner.
How long will you be over, Jo?
Oh, about 6 weeks, give or take.

I'm going to miss you. But before you leave we're going to have one more record date. This is Monday. We're going to have a record date Wednesday with the great George Barnes and the great Rube Brown is going to be on that date. JONES: Well, that'll be all right. Who's the piano, Hank Jones and whoever, I don't remember now, but it's going to be a great session. We're looking forward to doing this thing. Harry Lim which is going to produce it, which is a great responsibility. Was that Keynote Jazz many years ago?
Yes, you see, because we must remember, Milt, that we were going through a lot of social changes at the
period when Harry Lim came in. We must remember that we were going through a war period.
